evidence: Read CONTEXT whole first ('Before you begin': read-this-page, get-clear, the safe-place paragraph, deciding-to-do-it, new-to-this, let-your-response-guide-you). The draft is the last sentence of the safe-place paragraph and appears once: 'If you are already partially or fully opened, use the later 'Already open? Contain before you deepen' section to help orient yourself, but do not attempt to deepen yourself if you are not stable.' COMPARISON WITH THE REPLACED WORDS: the draft differs from them only by dropping 'you can' ('you can use' becomes 'use'); every other word, including the heading's own words, 'later' and 'not stable', is the replaced sentence's. So it does what the_change says in letter (heading words, later and not stable are present, you can is gone), but it is a two-word edit, not a recast. I cannot see sample ci and nothing in the draft is visibly Emulate's, so it should be shown to the author as exactly that small edit and not described as a rewrite. MEANING: kept (use the later section to orient, do not deepen while unstable, which is the 'orientation, not permission to intensify an unstable state' of the source); 'use' for 'you can use' turns an offer into an instruction, which suits a safety line and matches the imperatives beside it ('get some immediate support', 'Put yourself in a place'); no new claim, fact, study or personal detail. SEAM: the sentence mirrors the one just above it ('If you are intoxicated, acutely confused...') in construction and formality, so it reads as part of the same run of precautions; the formal 'do not' against the earlier contracted 'Don't do this' and the quote marks around the heading (the neighbouring 'Come all the way back page' has none) are differences the replaced words already had, not introduced here. TELLS: checked T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the literal draft in context. One row is PRESENT in form: T02, at paragraph scale (four consecutive one-job precautions: the place, the activities to avoid, intoxication or confusion, already being open). I do not accept the writer's ledger line that it is not part of a run. It is justified because they are separate safety conditions the reader has to check one by one, the cadence is the paragraph's existing one, and this sentence replaces one beat with one beat, adds none, and is a long two-clause sentence rather than a compressed command. No other row PRESENT. Looked at and cleared: T10 and T22 (the 'you can' permission and coach wording is gone; what is left is an instruction with a reason, 'if you are not stable'); T11 and T19 (the pointer is a cross-reference but it carries the safety condition, so it is not a bare connective or announcement); T12 (partially or fully is an inclusive range, and use but do not is the plain permitted-versus-forbidden form of a precaution); T21 (the two clauses are one safety thought); T26 (the echo of deepen from the heading into the caution is deliberate in a safety line); T29 (the last clause adds the 'if you are not stable' condition rather than restating); C02 (the section is named by its heading, and 'yourself' is the reader). LINTER: 'D9 follows the source order' is trivially true of one sentence whose order (condition, permitted action, limit) is set by the safety logic, and T13 and T09 do not apply to a single-sentence change; accepted on the context. I do not rely on the writer's stated reason for it, which cites asides ('if I can put it that way', 'of course', 'just', '!') that are not in this draft. 'E36/E41 heavy second person' (8.8 per 100): the three 'you' are the opening condition, the condition in the caution, and one inside the heading's own words; the guide addresses the reader as 'you' throughout and this is a precaution, not a run of coaching lines; accepted.
